question.text: A 12% convertible bond of face value INR 1,000 has a conversion ratio of 25:1. If market price of the equity is INR 40 on the conversion date, what is the intrinsic equity value of the conversion option (excluding any bond value)?

explanation.text: The Logic: 25 shares * INR 40/share = INR 1,000, exactly equal to the bond face value. Conversion is AT-THE-MONEY; the option has only time value, no intrinsic premium to either party. The Trap: Option A is just the share price; options B and C are arbitrary distractors that do not match the conversion math. Note: The conversion ratio of 25:1 at INR 40 yields INR 1,000, exactly equal to the bond face value — the convertible is fairly priced at conversion, with no intrinsic premium to either party.
